limitations: F1 — Counterevidence: Moment lemmas and Theorem1.1(i) explicitly retain p<min(p*,2); a smaller positive exponent can preserve qualitative averaging.
F2 — Counterevidence: Actual Boltzmann functions are nonnegative; application selects m(lambda)=(b-a)/n, the corrected direction.
F3 — Counterevidence: Core weak-disorder proof uses TheoremB(i), not this branch.
F4 — Counterevidence: Nonconstant finite-support positive-beta laws have finite p* by rare high-weight box events; TheoremsD/E then give the checked strict improvement.
F5 — Counterevidence: Remark1.7 correctly uses mu_(n-1) and W_(n-1).
F6 — Counterevidence: TheoremE p24 uses correct bounded interval; later cited general-environment results remove this special condition.
F7 — Counterevidence: After using the parity lattice, quadratic lower bound and inverse covariance, the uniform coarse n^(-d/2) orders persist.
Limitations: No writes, compilation, rendering, image viewing, author-code execution, human review or backend verification.

Counterevidence: Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 1.1(i) only supply auxiliary moments below p* wedge 2, whereas the proof on pp.18–19 chooses them near the full p*. The literal singleton statement is not declared false by a spread-out witness. Correctly bounded moments can still yield positive qualitative decay.

Counterevidence: Actual Boltzmann factors are nonnegative and p.16 chooses the correct drift (b-a)/n. Thus these examples do not refute the correctly directed positive comparison used by the core proof.
Counterevidence: The main weak-disorder proof uses B(i), not B(ii).
Counterevidence: This checks the intended nondegenerate finite-P improvement when the stated external hypercontractivity and comparison theorem hold; it does not establish a failure there.
Counterevidence: Remark 1.7 consistently uses mu_(n-1) and W_(n-1).
Counterevidence: In a lattice basis, quadratic lower bound and correct inverse covariance retain the coarse n^(-d/2) orders, uniformly on the compact tilt cube.
Limit: The full phase-transition literature, hypercontractivity, all large-deviation machinery and the full moderate-deviation local-limit remainder theorem were not independently reconstructed.
Not performed: Every external phase-transition theorem not re-proved.
Not performed: Full Ahlswede-Gacs hypercontractivity result, Lawler-Limic moderate-deviation remainder theorem, and all large-deviation machinery not independently reconstructed.
Not performed: Human review, author-code execution, and publisher-PDF comparison were not performed.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
The stated averaging result supplies the spread-out random endpoint law and full-p* rate.

Uniform bridge ratio for all real measurable functions under printed drift condition.

Strong disorder implies positive liminf of maximal next-step endpoint probability.

Strict p* monotonicity for every finite-support law with p*>1.

mu_(omega,n)(X_n=x)=W_pinned/W_n times SRW probability.

P(omega<=K)=0 for some K>0 expresses upper boundedness.

Scaled two-step walk is Zd-valued; covariance controls linear norm below; Fourier exponent contains covariance instead of inverse.
